title: Stalks of the inverse image of a sheaf along a continuous map, with germs
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces and let $\mathcal C$ be the category of abelian groups or the category of commutative rings. For a sheaf $\mathcal G$ on $Y$ with values in $\mathcal C$ let $f^{-1}\mathcal G$ be its inverse image, the sheafification of the presheaf $f_p\mathcal G:U\mapsto\varinjlim_{V\supseteq f(U)}\mathcal G(V)$, and let $\eta_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to f_*f^{-1}\mathcal G$ be the unit of the adjunction $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ (so $\eta_{\mathcal G,V}:\mathcal G(V)\to(f^{-1}\mathcal G)(f^{-1}V)$ for $V\subseteq Y$ open). Then for every $x\in X$, with $y=f(x)$, there is an isomorphism in $\mathcal C$
$$c_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G_y\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }(f^{-1}\mathcal G)_x,$$
natural in $\mathcal G$, such that $c_{\mathcal G}(s_y)=(\eta_{\mathcal G,V}(s))_x$ for every open $V\ni y$ and every $s\in\mathcal G(V)$. In particular every element of $(f^{-1}\mathcal G)_x$ is the germ at $x$ of $\eta_{\mathcal G,V}(s)$ for some open $V\ni y$ and some $s\in\mathcal G(V)$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma Tag 008H (label lemma-stalk-pullback: $(f^{-1}\mathcal G)_x=\mathcal G_{f(x)}$), proved from Lemma Tag 008G (lemma-stalk-pullback-presheaf, the colimit computation $(f_p\mathcal G)_x=\varinjlim_{x\in U}\varinjlim_{f(U)\subseteq V}\mathcal G(V)=\mathcal G_{f(x)}$) and stalks commute with sheafification (lemma-stalk-sheafification); the germ formula is the construction (the map $\mathcal G(V)\to f_p\mathcal G(f^{-1}V)$ is the presheaf unit)
